newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cadbury sweetens with value pledge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cadbury sweetens with value pledge.

text.p: Cadbury Schweppes Plc pleased investors on Wednesday with a new commitment to shareholder value plus a convincing picture of growth potential for its soft drinks and confectionery businesses, analysts said.
The company's move to change its long term incentive plan to align management motivation more closely with shareholder interests was taken very positively by the market, they said.
Cadbury's shares raced ahead to close 18 pence higher at 528 pence.
The British sweets and soft drinks group also succeeded in soothing fears about intense competition in the U.S. soft drinks market, where Cadbury is up against Coca-Cola and Pepsi.
"They have acknowledged they are in the ring with a couple of fearsome opponents," said David Laing at Henderson Crosthwaite, but they are saying that they can deal with it.
Cadbury revealed its plans as it reported a 16 percent increase in profits for 1996.
Chief executive John Sunderland acknowledged business was tough, but said Cadbury had a history of thriving in competitive markets.

The firm also seemed to convince investors that its U.S. distribution and bottling operations -- its so-called route to the market -- was secure, despite some of its minor brands being delisted last year by Coca-Cola.
Sunderland said the group was convinced that for the medium- to long-term its Dr Pepper brand had a secure place in all its routes to market in the United States.
"The company has strongly come out to allay fears over the U.S. route to market," said Ian Kellett, food manufacturing analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
Lang said the runup in the share price could continue if Cadbury maintained satisfactory sales in North America.
"If Cadbury holds its own against Coke and Pepsi there's more to go for," he said.
Chairman Dominic Cadbury told reporters that a strong cashflow, bolstered by the sale last month of its stake in Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages, gave it room to look for other acquisitions.

"If an opportunity comes along we're in a good position to finance an acquisition...from within our own resources," he said, adding that the group had the capacity to spend between one and two billion pounds ($3.2 billion). ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
